gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Raw, scattered, loud: Disorder spaces its big lowercase well apart. Noto Sans Lisu is the sans-serif that holds still, its s curves wide open and its ascenders nearly touching the x-height line.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Disorder draws round bowls whose walls never swell anywhere. It is at its best loud and spread out, whereas Noto Sans Lydian is at its best friendly and tame, with capitals barely taller than lowercase.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-mro: Disorder bends its letters like paperclip wire, with no swelling at any joint. Noto Sans Mro keeps paragraphs modern and dense through the middle of each word, with big openings into every letter.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-multani: Noto Sans Multani lifts its x-height high and leaves a wide gap at the e terminal. But Disorder is the wilder one, flat in weight and loose in spacing, so shrinking it wastes that rawness.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-nabatae: Loud and loose, Disorder spaces its big lowercase far apart, diagonals matching horizontals. Yet Noto Sans Nabataean, a sans-serif with lowercase almost cap-tall, steadies it, and that gap in temperament is the draw.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-nag-mun: Noto Sans Nag Mundari reads contemporary, its curls half unwrapped and its lowercase rivaling the capitals. Disorder can take the loud end, so give it room and let the sans-serif stay quiet below.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-nandina: Disorder scatters its big lowercase and keeps diagonals and horizontals alike in weight. Noto Sans Nandinagari is the approachable sans-serif, short in the ascenders and generous in its openings at every weight.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-newa: Disorder is best at being raw, joining strokes without thinning or bulging. Noto Sans Newa is best at being quiet, a modern sans with an open-mouthed e and tall bowls.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Raw and spaced out, Disorder draws every stroke like a stylus held at fixed pressure. Yet Noto Sans Nushu stands tower-tall in sans-serif form, its terminals held far from the stroke body.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-ol-chik: Glass tubing bent into letters: that is Disorder, spaced wide and raw. Noto Sans Ol Chiki reads clean and contemporary, in solid blocks rather than skylines, its curve tails held well back.
